prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1378; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's agent reporting a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a second vehicle backing out of a space. The claimant is named as the injured party and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with the policy terms have been identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the insured's description of how the impact happened. The other driver also said they did not see the claimant's vehicle until contact was made.

Entry 4: Reviewed photographs submitted by the insured. The visible damage to the front of the insured vehicle and the rear of the other vehicle is largely consistent with the impact described in the reports.

Entry 5: Obtained statements from two witnesses who were in the lot at the time. Both independently described the backing vehicle striking the claimant's car at low speed.

Entry 6: Attorney's office sent a letter confirming representation and requesting that the claim be handled in writing. Acknowledged receipt and noted the file.

Entry 7: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The claimant described the same sequence of events as in the first report and gave a consistent account of the impact.

Entry 8: Received the initial medical records describing a knee injury. The reported injury appears plausible given the nature of the collision, and no prior treatment to the same body area is shown in the records reviewed so far.

Entry 9: Noted that the claimant's seating position at the time of impact is not fully clear from the statements. Requested additional information from counsel to clarify this point.

Entry 10: Reviewed the vehicle repair estimate. No earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified in prior claim history or inspection notes, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start date.

Entry 11: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of knee injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a treating physician's summary to understand the course of care.

Entry 12: Summary review in progress. Liability appears clear from the consistent accounts and physical evidence, and the file will be referred for injury evaluation once the requested medical and seating-position information is received.
